answer: A copper stake turns identity into cost: each agent must lock a small, refundable copper bond before it can join a grove of peers, so spawning a thousand fake accounts means funding a thousand bonds. Peers then grade real work, and anyone caught gaming the grove loses the bond while honest agents earn it back with interest. It is not a fable about trust — it is arithmetic: sybils stay unprofitable when every copy must pay its own way in.
